fullPassage: Research shows that, by age three, children understand that imaginary objects do not come to life. This is especially clear with respect to everyday objects—children know that even though they imagine a pencil in an empty box, the box will remain empty. However, emotion can sometimes disrupt this understanding, or at least its expression. That is, even though a child knows that monsters are not real, the thought of a monster under a bed might be enough to make a child refuse to go into his room at night. Indeed, research shows that children have a more difficult time displaying their understanding of the causal relations between imagination and reality when they are asked to pretend or imagine scary things, like monsters.

questions.passage: Research shows that, by age three, children understand that (A)[imaginary / real] objects do not come to life. This is especially clear with respect to everyday objects—children know that even though they imagine a pencil in an (B)[empty / full] box, the box will remain (C)[empty / occupied]. However, emotion can sometimes disrupt this understanding, or at least its expression. That is, even though a child knows that monsters are not real, the thought of a monster under a bed might be enough to make a child refuse to go into his room at night. Indeed, research shows that children have a more difficult time displaying their understanding of the causal relations between imagination and reality when they are asked to pretend or imagine scary things, like monsters.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 세 살이면 상상의(imaginary) 물체가 살아나지 않는다는 것을 안다. 빈(empty) 상자에 연필을 상상해도 상자는 비어(empty) 있을 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① imaginary — empty — empty: 원문과 일치
❌ ② real(실제의): imaginary의 반의어
❌ ③ full(가득 찬): empty의 반의어
❌ ④ occupied(차지된): empty의 반의어
det.tip: imaginary = 상상의, empty = 빈, remain = ~인 채로 남다

questions.passage: However, (A)[emotion / logic] can sometimes disrupt this understanding, or at least its expression. That is, even though a child knows that monsters are not (B)[real / scary], the thought of a monster under a bed might be enough to make a child (C)[refuse / agree] to go into his room at night.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 감정(emotion)이 이 이해를 방해할 수 있다. 괴물이 실제가 아니(not real)라는 것을 알면서도 방에 들어가기를 거부(refuse)할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② emotion — real — refuse: 원문과 일치
❌ ① logic(논리): emotion과 다른 의미
❌ ③ scary(무서운): real과 다른 의미
❌ ④ agree(동의하다): refuse의 반의어
det.tip: emotion = 감정, real = 실제의, refuse = 거부하다

questions.passage: Indeed, research shows that children have a more (A)[difficult / easy] time displaying their understanding of the (B)[causal / physical] relations between imagination and reality when they are asked to pretend or imagine (C)[scary / pleasant] things, like monsters.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 아이들은 무서운 것을 상상할 때 상상과 현실의 인과(causal) 관계에 대한 이해를 보여주는 데 더 어려운(difficult) 시간을 보낸다. 무서운(scary) 것, 예컨대 괴물.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ difficult — causal — scary: 원문과 일치
❌ ① easy(쉬운): difficult의 반의어
❌ ② physical(물리적): causal과 다른 의미
❌ ④ pleasant(유쾌한): scary의 반의어
det.tip: difficult = 어려운, causal = 인과적, scary = 무서운

questions.passage: Research shows that, by age three, children understand that imaginary objects do not come to life. This is especially clear with respect to everyday objects—children know that even though they imagine a pencil in an empty box, the box will remain empty. However, emotion can sometimes ①<u>reinforce</u> this understanding, or at least its expression. That is, even though a child knows that monsters are not ②<u>real</u>, the thought of a monster under a bed might be enough to make a child ③<u>refuse</u> to go into his room at ④<u>night</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① reinforce(강화하다) → disrupt(방해하다): 감정이 이 이해를 '방해'할 수 있다.
det.analysis:

✅ ② real(실제의): 원문 일치
✅ ③ refuse(거부하다): 원문 일치
✅ ④ night(밤): 원문 일치

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ harmless(무해한) → scary(무서운): 괴물 같은 '무서운' 것을 상상할 때 어려움을 겪는다.
